svg.text: Flotsam Cage – Plan and Nested Cutting Layout
Flotsam cage – plan from above, and cutting layout from a single sheet
One sheet cuts the 11 beams for one side of the cage.
2 sheets per cage. Waste between nests is re-granulated.
INDICATIVE ARTIST'S ILLUSTRATION – NOT TO SCALE
Dimensions to be confirmed by survey and detailed design
The 'viking boat' form is made entirely from horizontal beams. Each course is a curved plank; the courses shorten and narrow with depth to form the hull.
All 11 courses are cut from one flat sheet of recycled plastic, nested crown-to-crown to minimise waste. Both sides use the same 9 shapes, so 2 sheets make one cage.
Sheet: 4 200 x 2 800 x 19 mm. Cut on a CNC router; edges eased 3 mm radius. Offcut between nests is returned for re-granulation.
Beams are laid flat, 150 mm face horizontal and 19 mm on edge, with a 150 mm clear slot between courses. Bolted through to the steel frame at every rib — see Drawing 6.
Plan shows courses nested inside one another as seen from above; the gunwale course is the outermost line.
Nesting shown is indicative. Final nest to be set from the sheet size actually supplied and the CNC bed.
